kz_kura.gf_detail: A hand-cut soba house — but not celiac-safe by default. Soba is usually cut nihachi-style with ~20% wheat flour, the dipping tsuyu is built on wheat soy sauce, and udon (pure wheat) is made in the same kitchen, so cross-contact is likely. Ask directly before ordering.
kz_kura.vegan_detail: The soba tsuyu and broths use katsuo/fish dashi, and the signature bowl is duck (kamo). A plain cold seiro soba might be possible but the dipping sauce is fish-based — confirm with staff.
kz_kura.hours_raw: Mon 11:00–15:00 (no dinner); Tue closed; Wed–Sun 11:00–15:00 & 17:30–20:00. Closes early once the day’s soba sells out.
kz_kura.notes: [Mom & Pop] A quiet hand-pulled soba shop on a back street in the historic Shimoshinmachi district, east of Omichō — a locals’ favorite known among those in the know, balancing serious craft with everyday prices.

chef_bio.background: A hand-pulled soba shop tucked down a quiet back street in Shimoshinmachi, one of Kanazawa's historic neighborhoods near the Izumi Kyōka Memorial Hall, a short walk east of Omichō Market. The buckwheat is milled in-house from whole grain sourced in Fukui and Hokkaidō.
chef_bio.philosophy: Serious craft at an everyday price — the kind of unshowy neighborhood soba-ya that locals quietly champion.
chef_bio.specialty: Hand-cut soba with a firm chew and pronounced buckwheat aroma; the signature bowl is kamo-nanban (warm soba with duck and leek). Udon is also on the menu.

anecdotes.text: The shop mills its own buckwheat from whole grain grown in Fukui and Hokkaidō, and is known for closing early once the day's soba runs out.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: いいじ金沢 confirms 下新町・泉鏡花記念館近く、玄そばからの自家製粉（福井・北海道産）、鴨南蛮（¥1,050）が看板、うどんもあり、売り切れ次第終了、手打ちの強いコシと蕎麦の旨味.

gf_cross_contamination.text: Wheat-flour udon is made in the same kitchen and soba is typically cut with some wheat, so gluten cross-contact is likely.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: Soba tsuyu / dipping sauce is based on wheat-containing soy sauce.

vegan_cross_contact.text: Broths and tsuyu use fish (katsuo) dashi; the signature bowl is duck.

cultural_comfort.note: A quiet neighborhood soba-ya loved by locals; a little Japanese (or pointing at the kamo-nanban) and an arrive-early-before-soba-sells-out mindset will serve you well.

kz_conconto.gf_detail: [Adversarial GF review 2026-08-19: dedicated→options. Identity confirmed (石川県金沢市横川5-267, 代表 大平弘二, opened May 2017) and the shop is still trading, but I disproved the label's central premise. The record's whole case rests on a 2017 Kanazawa Keizai Shimbun article quoting 「全商品…特定原材料7品目は使わず、米や豆など植物性の食材のみでつくる」 — and the shop's OWN PR Times release of 2025-10-02 states 「2025年からは乳製品・卵も取り入れた『Oishii糀スイーツ』シリーズを本格展開」 with a product whose 主な原材料 are 脱脂粉乳, 北海道産生クリーム, 米粉 and 卵. Two of the 7 designated allergens are therefore now handled in that kitchen, so the inference 'wheat is never present on site' no longer follows, and no current wheat/gluten statement, no celiac-grade listing (not on the japan-glutenfree.com all-GF bakery list, no HappyCow/FindMeGlutenFree celiac review) corroborates it. Rice-flour sweets almost certainly remain, so options — not dedicated.] A rice-flour patisserie and cafe. The 2017 all-plant, 7-allergen-free description below is SUPERSEDED: the shop’s own 2025-10-02 PR Times release announces an 「Oishii糀スイーツ」 line built with 脱脂粉乳, 生クリーム and 卵, so dairy and egg are now handled in that kitchen. The shop states 「全商品、卵や乳製品、小麦粉、そば、落花生など食物アレルギー物質の特定原材料7品目は使わず、米や豆など植物性の食材のみでつくる」 (all products use none of the 7 major allergens — egg, dairy, wheat flour, soba, peanut, etc. — only plant-based ingredients like rice and beans). That kitchen no longer excludes all seven designated allergens, so the "nothing risky is ever present" inference no longer holds. Confirm the specific item with staff.
kz_conconto.vegan_detail: [Corrected 2026-08-19] No longer fully vegan: the shop's own 2025-10-02 release introduces an 「Oishii糀スイーツ」 range using 脱脂粉乳 (skim milk powder), 生クリーム (cream) and 卵 (egg). The original rice-and-bean range appears to continue, so vegan items exist — but the menu as a whole is not vegan. Ask which line an item belongs to. Everything is vegan by design — the shop describes itself as making sweets 「米粉と植物性食材のみでつくる」 (only from rice flour and plant-based ingredients). Dairy is replaced with soy-milk-based ice cream and custard; eggs are not used at all. Whole menu is safe for vegans.
kz_conconto.notes: [GF-dedicated] A rare 100% wheat-free patisserie in Kanazawa: all cakes, tarts, Mont Blanc and parfaits are built from rice flour and beans, with no wheat, buckwheat or peanut anywhere in the kitchen. This is one of the safest cafe stops in the region for celiacs, and it doubles as a plant-based cafe (soy-milk ice cream, custard). Sit-in seating (~8 seats) means you can enjoy a parfait or cake with Kaga bōcha tea on the spot.

chef_bio.background: Yamazaki worked in Western pastry manufacturing and production management before handling sales for his family's Kaga lacquerware wholesale house (山崎又一商店). In 2014 he launched the project unit 'Conconto' to promote traditional Ishikawa crafts such as Yamanaka lacquerware, and the patisserie opened in May 2017 as a food-culture arm of that project. The shop occupies a converted 1960s fiber-machinery building near the Yokogawa intersection in southern Kanazawa, with a small ~8-seat café. His stated aim is to convey the food culture handed down through generations by making authentic Western sweets from the rice and beans Japanese have long eaten.
chef_bio.philosophy: Make authentic Western-style confectionery from rice, beans and other plant ingredients — kind to allergy sufferers and the body alike, excluding the 7 major allergen categories and minimizing food additives.
chef_bio.specialty: Rice-flour and bean-based cakes, tarts, chestnut Mont Blanc and seasonal parfaits (plant-based and free of the 7 major allergens, per the shop).

anecdotes.text: The pastry shop grew out of Yamazaki's 'Conconto' craft-promotion project (est. 2014), tying Ishikawa's lacquerware heritage to a new food venture.
From 2025 the shop began incorporating kōji (糀) fermentation into its sweets — including a koji cheesecake and an 'umami' roll cake made with rice-koji-fermented milk paste.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 金沢経済新聞 confirms 山崎弘二が運営、洋菓子製造・生産管理の経歴と家業（加賀の漆器卸 山崎又一商店）、2014年『コンコント』プロジェクト、2017年5月開店、横川の元繊維機械会社ビル（約15坪・8席）、米と豆の植物性素材で7大アレルゲン不使用・添加物を極力使わない; PR TIMES confirms 2025年から糀発酵を取り入れた新商品展開.

gf_cross_contamination.text: 全商品、卵や乳製品、小麦粉、そば、落花生など食物アレルギー物質の特定原材料7品目は使わず、米や豆など植物性の食材のみでつくる — no wheat, soba or peanut is present anywhere in production, so cross-contact risk is minimal.
gf_cross_contamination.source_wording: 全商品、卵や乳製品、小麦粉、そば、落花生など食物アレルギー物質の特定原材料7品目は使わず、食品添加物はできるだけ使わず、ヘルシーで体に負担の少ないケーキや焼き菓子を用意する。／（別文）金沢・横川交差点近くに、米や豆など植物性食材だけで作る洋菓子の店「コンコント菓子店」

soy_sauce_wheat.text: Dessert-only patisserie; no soy sauce used in the sweets menu.

vegan_cross_contact.text: Entirely plant-based kitchen — dairy replaced by soy-milk ice cream and custard, no eggs used, so vegan cross-contact is not a concern.

staff_allergy_handling.text: Shop is explicitly built around allergy safety, making items suitable for people with allergies as well as those without.

positives.text: 100% wheat-free, buckwheat-free and peanut-free dedicated plant-based patisserie with sit-in cafe — a standout safe option in Kanazawa.

gf_review.why: Identity confirmed (石川県金沢市横川5-267, 代表 大平弘二, opened May 2017) and the shop is still trading, but I disproved the label's central premise. The record's whole case rests on a 2017 Kanazawa Keizai Shimbun article quoting 「全商品…特定原材料7品目は使わず、米や豆など植物性の食材のみでつくる」 — and the shop's OWN PR Times release of 2025-10-02 states 「2025年からは乳製品・卵も取り入れた『Oishii糀スイーツ』シリーズを本格展開」 with a product whose 主な原材料 are 脱脂粉乳, 北海道産生クリーム, 米粉 and 卵. Two of the 7 designated allergens are therefore now handled in that kitchen, so the inference 'wheat is never present on site' no longer follows, and no current wheat/gluten statement, no celiac-grade listing (not on the japan-glutenfree.com all-GF bakery list, no HappyCow/FindMeGlutenFree celiac review) corroborates it. Rice-flour sweets almost certainly remain, so options — not dedicated.
red_flags: Shop's own 2025 press release confirms it now uses 乳製品 and 卵 — the '7 allergens never enter this kitchen' basis for the dedicated label is factually obsolete
gf_detail currently asserts 'no wheat is used or baked anywhere on site' and 'cross-contact risk is very low' — an active over-claim that must be rewritten
vegan_status 'full' is now FALSE (dairy + egg line since 2025) — separate safety-relevant error outside the GF tier
All evidence in the record dates to 2017; nothing post-dates the 2025 product-line change
No celiac-grade corroboration found anywhere; not on the national all-GF bakery list
Unconfirmed chatter about a relocation from the Yokogawa site — could not verify either way
gf_review.plain_rice: No — patisserie/cafe only, no plain gohan served.

kz_kamuna.gf_detail: A tiny container-house 'natural sweets' workshop making 米粉・もち粉 (rice-flour/mochi-flour) treats like the signature カムナどらやき (fermented-anko dorayaki). Most days are wheat-free, but LOWERED from options because the owner intentionally uses wheat: her site states 「普段小麦粉は使用いたしませんが」 and 「グルテンフリー（日曜日はスペルト小麦使用）」— 「日曜日のみ不定期で『スペルト小麦（古代小麦）』を使用した『小麦に感謝の日』を開催いたします」(on some Sundays she holds a 'day of gratitude to wheat' using spelt). Spelt IS wheat/gluten and is baked in the same small shared kitchen, so cross-contact is a real risk and no wheat-free-kitchen claim or protocol is published. The shop's 'グルテンフリー' wording is a health-lifestyle framing, not a celiac guarantee — ask directly about same-day/same-equipment wheat handling before eating.
kz_kamuna.vegan_detail: Not vegan. Products rely on egg for leavening — 「卵の力で膨らませられるようレシピを作りました」(uses Noto/Ishikawa cage-free eggs) — and use butter: 「乳製品はバターのみ使用」. No vegan line is offered, though white sugar is often omitted (「お砂糖不使用です！」on some items).
kz_kamuna.hours_raw: Tue/Thu/Sat 11:00–18:00; Sunday irregular ~9:00–13:00 (often the spelt 'wheat gratitude day' — avoid for celiacs); closed Mon/Wed/Fri plus irregular closures. Only ~3 days/week — check Instagram @kamuna357 / LINE calendar before visiting.
kz_kamuna.notes: [GF] Rice-flour natural-sweets shop, NOT celiac-safe as-is: the owner deliberately bakes spelt (古代小麦) on some Sundays in the same tiny kitchen and publishes no cross-contact controls. Products also contain egg and butter (not vegan). If visiting, avoid Sundays, and message @kamuna357 or LINE beforehand to confirm the day's items are wheat-free and how equipment is handled. Open only ~3 days/week; check the daily calendar. Phone 070-8948-3496.

chef_bio.background: The owner is a former nurse (元看護師) and mother who started Kamuna during the pandemic (opened Jan 11, 2022) out of a preventive-medicine conviction — wanting healthy snacks she would feel good feeding her own children, priced so kids can buy them with their own pocket money. She cites rising childhood allergies, mental illness and cancer as part of what drove her, and uses pesticide-free Ishikawa rice flour (無農薬米粉), mochi flour, Ishikawa free-range eggs, and no white sugar (muscovado and organic maple instead) with no additives.
chef_bio.philosophy: Affordable, additive-free, mostly rice-flour 'natural sweets' for children's health — while keeping 'a relationship with wheat as an occasional indulgence' (「時々食べる嗜好品として小麦とお付き合いしていきます」), with spelt (ancient-wheat) scones and bread on occasional Sunday 'wheat gratitude' days.
chef_bio.specialty: カムナどらやき — dorayaki pairing a moist shiratamako (glutinous rice-flour) skin with a sugar-free koji-fermented anko; plus sesame brownies/pound cakes, sablé butter sandwiches and rice-flour tarts.

anecdotes.text: The shop name 'Kamuna' combines カタツムリ (snail, a happiness symbol) with 直江 (Naoe, the neighborhood); a snail motif marks the small container-house shop.
Owner is a former nurse who launched the shop so healthy snacks would be cheap enough for kids to buy with pocket money.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: manpuku・kaname・公式Wixサイト confirm 元看護師のオーナー、予防医療の動機、子供のアレルギー・精神疾患・癌が増えているという問題意識、カタツムリ＋直江の店名・スネイルロゴ、コンテナ店舗、無農薬米粉・大豆、放し飼い卵、白砂糖不使用（素焚糖・メープル）、発酵あんこ＋白玉粉のどらやき、駄菓子価格; Wix confirms 時々食べる嗜好品として小麦、日曜のスペルト小麦『感謝の日』。

gf_cross_contamination.text: Owner intentionally bakes spelt wheat (スペルト小麦/古代小麦) on some Sundays in the same small kitchen: 「日曜日のみ不定期で『スペルト小麦（古代小麦）』を使用した『小麦に感謝の日』を開催いたします」. Spelt is wheat/gluten; shared-equipment cross-contact is a real, uncontrolled risk.
No wheat-free-kitchen claim, no 'may contain' warning and no cross-contact protocol are published. Absence of a warning is not evidence of safety.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: Sweets shop; no soy sauce noted. Other allergens present: egg, butter (dairy), sesame, almond, cocoa, matcha.

vegan_cross_contact.text: Not vegan — egg is used for leavening and butter for dairy; no plant-based separation.

staff_allergy_handling.text: No published allergy-handling policy; owner reachable via Instagram @kamuna357 / LINE for questions.

positives.text: Most days' products are rice-flour/mochi-flour based (Ishikawa 無農薬米粉), additive-free with reduced/no white sugar.
Owner is health-focused (former nurse) and transparent about when wheat is used.

kz_komekura.gf_detail: A multi-purpose cafe run by the ~120-year-old Kurayama rice merchant in Hakusan City (just outside Kanazawa). Its flagship rice waffle is marketed as 「米粉を100%使用した完全グルテンフリースイーツ」(a completely gluten-free sweet using 100% rice flour), made with 白山市産米粉100% (100% Hakusan-grown rice flour). However this is a general cafe with heavy wheat use — four wheat pastas, hot sandwiches, bread/chili dog, and hayashi-rice roux (conventionally wheat-thickened). No allergen protocol, dedicated GF prep area or cross-contact statement is published anywhere, so the '完全グルテンフリー' claim refers to the waffle recipe, not a controlled process. Treat the venue as high cross-contamination risk and confirm handling with the shop before a celiac eats.
kz_komekura.vegan_detail: No vegan program or labeling. The flagship rice waffle is served with butter and honey; chocolate-banana waffle and cheesecake contain dairy. A few onigiri (塩 salt, 梅 umeboshi, 昆布 kombu) are incidentally plant-based but carry no allergen/ingredient guarantee (nori/seasonings unverified); the miso-soup set likely uses fish dashi.
kz_komekura.hours_raw: 9:30–17:00, Mon–Sat; closed Sundays and public holidays. Onigiri available from ~10:30.
kz_komekura.notes: [GF] The 100% rice-flour waffle is a genuine GF-recipe treat and the reason to come, but this is a wheat-heavy kitchen (pasta, hot sandwiches, bread, hayashi roux) with no published cross-contact controls. For a diagnosed celiac, phone ahead (076-259-1100) to confirm how the waffle is prepared and whether utensils/griddle are shared. Do not assume the venue itself is gluten-free; avoid the hayashi rice (roux is wheat-based). ~5–6 min walk from Mattō Station; 13-car parking.

chef_bio.background: Komekura Coffee is operated by 倉山米穀 (Kurayama Beikoku), a long-established (~120-year) family rice merchant. The cafe is framed as 「お米屋さんが提案する、魅力あふれる多目的カフェ」(an appealing multi-purpose cafe proposed by a rice merchant). It employs 石川県唯一の五ツ星お米マイスター — Ishikawa Prefecture's only Five-Star Rice Meister — whose expertise drives ingredient and menu selection. The shop is certified under Hakusan City's chisan-chisho (local-production) program.
chef_bio.philosophy: Showcase premium local rice: primarily Koshihikari (switching to new-crop/seasonal varieties), with self-made onigiri as the signature and 白山市産米粉100% sweets. Committed to the core ingredients 'rice and bread.'
chef_bio.specialty: Hand-made onigiri (several kinds) and 100% Hakusan rice-flour waffles; premium rice and goods sold on the ground floor.

anecdotes.text: A two-floor wood-and-steel cafe: the upper floor has lounge seating and billiards cues on display, with floor-to-ceiling windows looking onto the Shinkansen tracks; the barrier-free ground floor offers Wi-Fi and sells premium rice alongside Volkswagen-themed merchandise.
Menu selection is guided by the prefecture's only Five-Star Rice Meister employed by the shop.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 週末、金沢 establishes the ~120-year rice-merchant heritage, 石川県唯一の五ツ星お米マイスター、米粉100%の完全グルテンフリーワッフル、おにぎり; 白山市 confirms 白山市産米粉100%（地産地消）; ishikabakun covers the two-floor multi-purpose-cafe concept, 2階のビリヤードのキュー、大きな窓（新幹線ビュー）、1階のVWグッズと倉山米穀の米販売.

gf_cross_contamination.text: General cafe with heavy wheat use — 4 wheat pastas, hot sandwiches, bread and a chili dog — sharing the same kitchen as the rice waffle; no dedicated GF prep area or utensil separation is published.
No allergen or cross-contact statement appears in any source; the '完全グルテンフリー' label describes the waffle recipe only.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: Hayashi rice roux conventionally contains wheat flour — treat as NOT gluten-free despite being served over rice. Onigiri/miso-set seasonings and dashi are unverified for wheat.

vegan_cross_contact.text: Not vegan; butter, honey and dairy used across sweets. Any plant-based onigiri share a kitchen with meat fillings and wheat items.

staff_allergy_handling.text: No published allergy-handling policy; verify by phone (076-259-1100).

positives.text: Flagship waffle uses 白山市産米粉100% and is marketed as 「米粉を100%使用した完全グルテンフリースイーツ」.
Hakusan City government confirms the sweets use 100% Hakusan-grown rice flour (chisan-chisho certified).

kz_meringue.gf_detail: Novelty okonomiyaki bar whose batter uses beaten egg-white meringue instead of flour; the shop states 「小麦粉を一切使わず、メレンゲなどを使ったオリジナルの生地」 and reviewers confirm 「生地にメレンゲ使ってて小麦粉不使用でグルテンフリー！」 — the pancake batter itself is genuinely wheat-flour-free. Two open questions keep this at ask: (1) the finishing okonomiyaki ソース/オリジナルソース is not documented, and commercial okonomiyaki/tonkatsu-style sauce almost always contains wheat and soy sauce, so the sauce's celiac-safety is unverified; (2) it is a 鉄板バル that also cooks やきそば (wheat noodles) and offers a 「金澤野菜のサラダそば」 (soba, normally wheat-blended) on the same teppan, so shared-griddle cross-contact is real. Also note: Tabelog now tags the shop 【移転】 (relocated) and the official domain was unreachable at last check — verify the current location and sauce before visiting.
kz_meringue.vegan_detail: The signature is an egg-white-meringue okonomiyaki topped with 能登豚 (Noto pork), seafood (えび/かき) and dashi; the batter is egg-based by definition. No vegan offering.
kz_meringue.hours_raw: Approx. 11:30–14:30 and 17:30–21:00 (Tue 11:30–14:30; Sat 11:30–21:00; Sun/holidays 11:30–17:00); closed Wednesdays. Hours vary by day — shop advises checking Instagram (@meringue_1204). Older Tabelog listing shows 11:00–16:00.
kz_meringue.notes: [GF] The okonomiyaki batter is genuinely flourless (meringue, 小麦粉不使用), a rare celiac-friendly twist. But the finishing sauce is undocumented (okonomiyaki sauce usually contains wheat), the same teppan cooks やきそば/そば, and Tabelog flags the shop as relocated. Confirm current address, ask for the sauce ingredients (or bring/skip sauce), and request a clean griddle spot away from wheat noodles.

chef_bio.background: お好み焼き 鉄板バル メレンゲ opened on 4 December 2020 near the entrance to Omicho Market at 下堤町34-2, running as an okonomiyaki lunch spot by day and a 鉄板バル by night in an all-counter room. Its hook is a 'new-sensation' okonomiyaki that swaps wheat flour for whipped egg-white meringue, plated with Noto-brand pork and Kaga vegetables. Tabelog now flags the shop as relocated (【移転】) from that address, so its current base should be confirmed before visiting.
chef_bio.philosophy: Flourless, additive-free 'fluffy' okonomiyaki using local Ishikawa produce.
chef_bio.specialty: Meringue okonomiyaki (ぶた玉/えび玉/かき玉); teppan bar plates

anecdotes.text: The batter is whipped into a meringue so the okonomiyaki comes out unusually light and fluffy — reviewers describe it as 小麦粉不使用でグルテンフリー (note: sets are served with a soba-based salad, so anyone with celiac needs should confirm ingredients directly).
Daytime is an okonomiyaki shop; at night it flips to a teppan bar where all daytime drinks (including beer) are ¥300.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: kanazawadays.com confirms メレンゲ生地の小麦粉不使用お好み焼き（reviewers 曰くグルテンフリー）、2020年12月開業、下堤町34-2・近江町市場近く、能登豚・金澤野菜、セットに金澤野菜のサラダそば、昼お好み焼き/夜鉄板バル、全席カウンター; tacsp.net notes 昼ドリンク¥300; 食べログ lists the shop as 【移転】（旧住所 下堤町34-2）with no new address given.

gf_cross_contamination.text: It is a 鉄板バル cooking やきそば (wheat noodles) and a 「金澤野菜のサラダそば」 (soba, normally wheat-blended) on the same teppan as the flourless okonomiyaki — shared-griddle cross-contact is likely. All-counter room; no clean-surface protocol published.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: The finishing okonomiyaki ソース/オリジナルソース ingredients are undocumented. Standard okonomiyaki sauce contains wheat and soy sauce; no tamari/GF sauce is confirmed, so sauced okonomiyaki cannot be assumed gluten-free.

vegan_cross_contact.text: Egg-white-meringue batter plus pork/seafood — not vegan.

staff_allergy_handling.text: Shop markets the okonomiyaki as グルテンフリー based on the flourless batter, but no allergen/sauce/cross-contact statement is published; Tabelog flags the venue as relocated and the official domain was unreachable at last check.

positives.text: Genuinely flourless okonomiyaki — batter uses egg-white meringue instead of wheat flour (小麦粉不使用), a rare celiac-friendly base.

kz_miron.gf_detail: [Adversarial GF review 2026-08-19: dedicated→high. Identity confirmed (〒929-0323 河北郡津幡町津幡ニ504-1, tel 076-255-2382, opened May 2022, active on the Tsubata town business directory).
